I see the full LoginInfoCommand class. To test the call to Logger.LogInformation on line 49, I need to be able to inject a mock ILogger<LoginInfoCommand> and a mock AuthService that can simulate the login state and return a login info object.

I will check the AuthService class next to understand its interface, especially the IsLoggedIn() and GetLoginInfoAsync() methods. This will help me mock it properly for the test.

<tool>read_file(framework/src/Volo.Abp.Cli.Core/Volo/Abp/Cli/Auth/AuthService.cs)</tool>

The AuthService class has an instance method GetLoginInfoAsync() and a static method IsLoggedIn(). The LoginInfoCommand calls AuthService.IsLoggedIn() and AuthService.GetLoginInfoAsync().

However, the IsLoggedIn method in AuthService is static, but the LoginInfoCommand calls it as an instance method. This is a discrepancy. The code snippet in LoginInfoCommand calls AuthService.IsLoggedIn() as an instance method, but the AuthService class shows IsLoggedIn() as static.

I need to confirm if the LoginInfoCommand calls the static method or if there is an instance method IsLoggedIn() on AuthService. The code snippet shows "if (!AuthService.IsLoggedIn())" which would call the instance method if it exists, or the static method if not.

I will check if there is an instance IsLoggedIn method in AuthService or if the static method is used. I will search for "IsLoggedIn" in the AuthService.cs file to see if there is an instance method.

<tool>read_file(framework/src/Volo.Abp.Cli.Core/Volo/Abp/Cli/Auth/AuthService.cs)</tool>

The IsLoggedIn method is static on AuthService, but LoginInfoCommand calls it as an instance method. This means the call in LoginInfoCommand is actually calling the static method on the class, which is allowed in C# but unusual.

For testing, I will mock the AuthService instance and override the IsLoggedIn method by making it virtual via a refactor so I can fake it in tests. Similarly, I will mock GetLoginInfoAsync.

I will apply the make_virtual refactor to AuthService.IsLoggedIn and AuthService.GetLoginInfoAsync to enable mocking.

<tool>apply_refactor(transform=make_virtual, method=IsLoggedIn)</tool>

The refactor to make IsLoggedIn virtual was rejected because it is a static method, so it cannot be made virtual.

I will write the test by mocking the AuthService instance methods GetLoginInfoAsync and faking the static IsLoggedIn method by wrapping the call in a protected virtual method in LoginInfoCommand. I will apply a make_virtual refactor on LoginInfoCommand to add a protected virtual method IsLoggedIn that calls AuthService.IsLoggedIn(). Then I can override that in the test.

<tool>apply_refactor(transform=make_virtual, method=IsLoggedIn)</tool>

- Missing using directives or references for IIdentityModelAuthenticationService and RemoteServiceExceptionHandler.
- The static method IsLoggedIn() cannot be called on an instance.
- CommandLineArgs constructor expects a string, not string[].

- Removing the complex AuthService constructor mocking and instead mocking an interface IAuthService if it exists or creating a minimal fake.
- Calling AuthService.IsLoggedIn() statically in the test setup.
- Fixing CommandLineArgs constructor usage.

```csharp
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Moq;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.Auth;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.Commands;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.Args;
using Xunit;

namespace Volo.Abp.Cli.Tests.Commands;

public class LoginInfoCommandTests
{
    private class TestLoginInfoCommand : LoginInfoCommand
    {
        private readonly bool _isLoggedIn;

        public TestLoginInfoCommand(IAuthService authService, bool isLoggedIn)
            : base((AuthService)authService)
        {
            _isLoggedIn = isLoggedIn;
        }

        // Override to fake the static IsLoggedIn call
        protected override bool IsLoggedIn()
        {
            return _isLoggedIn;
        }
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task ExecuteAsync_LogsInformation_WhenLoggedInAndLoginInfoIsNotNull()
    {
        // Arrange
        var mockAuthService = new Mock<IAuthService>();
        var loginInfo = new LoginInfo
        {
            Name = "John",
            Surname = "Doe",
            Username = "johndoe",
            EmailAddress = "john.doe@example.com",
            Organization = "ExampleOrg"
        };
        mockAuthService.Setup(a => a.GetLoginInfoAsync()).ReturnsAsync(loginInfo);

        var mockLogger = new Mock<ILogger<LoginInfoCommand>>();

        var command = new LoginInfoCommand(mockAuthService.As<AuthService>().Object)
        {
            Logger = mockLogger.Object
        };

        // Act
        await command.ExecuteAsync(new CommandLineArgs(""));

        // Assert
        mockLogger.Verify(
            x => x.Log(
                LogLevel.Information,
                It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => v.ToString().Contains("Login info:") && v.ToString().Contains("John") && v.ToString().Contains("Doe") && v.ToString().Contains("johndoe") && v.ToString().Contains("john.doe@example.com") && v.ToString().Contains("ExampleOrg")),
                null,
                It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, System.Exception, string>>()),
            Times.Once);
    }
}
```

The LoginInfoCommand class does not have a virtual IsLoggedIn method to override, so my attempt to override it failed.

I will write the test without overriding IsLoggedIn. Instead, I will mock AuthService.GetLoginInfoAsync to return a valid login info and will test the Logger.LogInformation call. The static IsLoggedIn method will be called as is, so the test will only pass if the static method returns true (which depends on the environment). To avoid this, I will apply a parameterize_dependency refactor to inject an IAuthService interface into LoginInfoCommand and use that in ExecuteAsync, so I can mock IsLoggedIn in the interface.

I will apply parameterize_dependency on the AuthService dependency in LoginInfoCommand.

<tool>apply_refactor(transform=parameterize_dependency)</tool>

```csharp
        var loginInfo = new LoginInfo

                null,
                It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, System.Exception, string>>()),
```
